tagline: Old mill towns on the tidal rivers, Rollinsford to Newmarket.
intro: The byway starts at the South Berwick, Maine, line in Rollinsford, among eighteenth- and nineteenth-century farms, and follows Route 4 to the Dover line. It leaves a gap through Dover, easily bridged on Route 108, and picks up again in Madbury among old dairy-farm houses. Then 108 runs south through Durham and Newmarket to the Newfields line, crossing the Oyster River and the Lamprey, by white steeples and old mill buildings.

Within ten years of starting in the 1820s, the Salmon Falls Manufacturing Company in Rollinsford was weaving nearly 7 percent of the country's broadcloth. Newmarket built its cotton mills of granite instead of the usual brick.

moments.title: Rollinsford
moments.text: Here Route 4 runs alongside the Newichawannock trail, a Native American road older than 1600 that Revolutionary soldiers later traveled from Maine to Boston.

moments.title: Durham
moments.text: Route 108 crosses the Oyster River by Mill Pond, at the dam site where the Jenkins mill stood until decay and the weight of snow brought it down, reportedly about 1955.

moments.title: Newmarket
moments.text: The 2016 byway plan pointed out an old fishing weir in the tidal Lamprey, used by the Swamscott and early settlers, and the Macallen Dam and fish ladder seen from the bridge.

sources.label: Strafford Regional Planning Commission, Mills Scenic Byway Corridor Management Plan (2016)
